passage: Zainab saw it from the next bench in the village school's hall: Aditi, her best friend since Class 1, tucked a folded slip under her palm and copied the last two answers of the science paper. Nobody else noticed. All the way home along the canal path, Zainab's stomach twisted. Aditi kept talking about the buffalo calf as if nothing was wrong. At the tamarind tree, Zainab stopped. "I saw you today. The slip." Aditi went pale. "Please don't tell." "I'm not going to shout it," said Zainab. "But go to Sir yourself, before results. I can't pretend it didn't happen." Aditi kicked a stone and said nothing. "I'll wait for you at the gate tomorrow," Zainab added, and walked on, unsure whether they were still friends.

qa.q: Where did Zainab tell Aditi she had seen the slip?
qa.a: At the tamarind tree on the canal path home.

qa.q: What was Zainab feeling as she walked home, and what does it show?
qa.a: She felt torn between loyalty and honesty. Her stomach twisted, and she was unsure at the end whether they were still friends.

qa.q: What was wise in how Zainab responded to Aditi?
qa.a: She spoke privately, refused to pretend it hadn't happened, and urged Aditi to go to the teacher herself rather than joining in or staying silent.

qa.q: How might Aditi have felt when Zainab spoke to her?
qa.a: Frightened and ashamed. She went pale, begged Zainab not to tell, and kicked a stone in silence.

grounding: The protagonist knows her best friend cheated, urges her privately to come clean and refuses to be complicit.

passage: So you want the real story? Okay. I'm Gurleen, and last March I watched my best friend Yamini slide a folded chit out of her sock during the chemistry final. Nobody else saw. I did. For two days I couldn't eat properly. Part of me kept saying, she's your person, since class three, you don't do this to her. The other part kept seeing Farah, who studies till midnight and scored four marks less than Yamini. I didn't tell the teacher. I also didn't pretend it was fine. I waited till we were alone on the stairs and said, "I saw the chit. I'm not going to report you, but I can't act like I didn't see. Please tell Ma'am yourself." She cried, then got angry, then went quiet. When she offered me her chits for the physics paper, I said no. Did she confess? Not that week. But she stopped.

qa.q: What did Yamini take out of her sock during the chemistry final?
qa.a: Yamini slid a folded chit out of her sock during the chemistry final.

qa.q: What was Gurleen feeling in the two days after the exam?
qa.a: Gurleen felt torn and uneasy: loyalty to a friend since class three pulled one way, and fairness to Farah, who studied till midnight, pulled the other, so Gurleen could hardly eat.

qa.q: What did Gurleen get right in how the problem was handled?
qa.a: Gurleen spoke to Yamini privately, asked her to tell the teacher herself, and refused to join in when offered chits for the next paper.

qa.q: How might Yamini have seen that talk on the stairs?
qa.a: Yamini probably felt caught and hurt at first, which is why she cried and got angry, but she may also have felt that Gurleen was still on her side by not reporting her.

grounding: It shows a teen who knows a best friend copied, feels torn between loyalty and honesty, and privately urges the friend to come clean without joining in.

passage:
Monday. During the maths unit test, Chaitanya noticed Simran tilting her phone under the desk, the calculator app hiding a photo of the formula page. His stomach dropped. He looked away and finished his paper, hands cold.

Thursday. At the bus stop Simran laughed about her ninety-two. Chaitanya kept his voice low. "I saw your phone on Monday. I'm not telling anyone, but it wasn't fair to the rest of us. You should tell Mr D'Souza before the marks go on the board." Simran snapped that he was supposed to be her friend. He said, "I am. That's why I'm saying it to you and not about you."

The next Tuesday. Simran messaged him a photo of the formula page before the retest and wrote, "Just in case." Chaitanya deleted it without opening the full image and replied, "Not doing this. Want to revise together tonight instead?" After a long pause she sent, "Fine. Library, five o'clock."

qa.q: What was hidden behind the calculator app on Simran's phone?
qa.a: A photo of the formula page was hiding behind the calculator app.

qa.q: How can you tell Chaitanya felt uneasy on the Monday of the test?
qa.a: His stomach dropped and his hands went cold as he finished his paper, which shows anxiety about what he had seen and what to do about it.

qa.q: Which choice on the next Tuesday worked, and why?
qa.a: Deleting the photo and offering to revise together worked, because Chaitanya refused to join in while still offering Simran a fair way to prepare.

qa.q: What is it like for Simran when Chaitanya says he is speaking to her and not about her?
qa.a: It may sting because she feels caught, but it also shows her the friendship is still there, which may be why she later agrees to study at the library.

grounding: It shows the loyalty-versus-honesty pull over several days, with the friend urged privately to come clean and the protagonist refusing to join in.
